summary.text: Kristen Gonzalez is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for re-election to New York State Senate District 59, running unopposed. Raised in Queens, she worked as a staffer for the New York City Council, the Obama White House and Senator Chuck Schumer's office and as a tech worker before winning the seat in 2022. She chairs the Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Internet and Technology Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Queens, New York, and raised in a working-class family; lives in Long Island City. According to her campaign website, she was raised in Elmhurst, Queens, by a single mother from Puerto Rico after her father, who was from Colombia, died.
Graduated from Columbia University. According to her campaign website, she left college to work in Washington, D.C., and finished her degree after returning to New York.
Worked as a legislative staffer for the New York City Council, the Obama White House, and Senator Chuck Schumer's office before running for office.
According to her campaign website, she worked in tech as a product manager after returning to New York.
Organized with the Western Queens Community Land Trust, served on her local community board, and helped launch a citywide campaign for public internet.

Won the Democratic primary for State Senate District 59 on August 23, 2022, with 57.8% of the vote, defeating Elizabeth Crowley, Michael Corbett and others; won the November 8, 2022 general election with the Democratic and Working Families lines and took office January 1, 2023.
Won re-election in 2024, defeating Gus Lambropoulos in the June 25, 2024 Democratic primary.
The youngest woman ever elected to the New York State Senate, according to her official Senate biography.

Chairs the Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Internet and Technology Committee in the 2025–2026 session; also a member of the Children and Families, Consumer Protection, Energy and Telecommunications, Health and Rules committees and the Legislative Women's Caucus.
Her legislative work includes protecting private health data to safeguard abortion rights, regulating government use of artificial intelligence, and protecting elections from deceptive media.
